messages.text: Thinking about getting more serious about wine. Is it worth taking a WSET 1 course or just reading on my own?

Depends on how you learn. WSET 1 is structured, tasting-led, and gets you a vocabulary fast — and the tutor format keeps you accountable. If you're disciplined and have access to a varied wine retailer, reading along with regular blind tastings at home gets you maybe 80% of the way for free. Most people do better with the class for the social aspect alone.
Catch is — I have a sulfite allergy. Most wine has added sulfites, which puts me out of all but the natural-wine corner of the market. Doesn't make me a great wine student.

That changes the math a bit. Natural wine is its own subculture with passionate practitioners but a narrower vocabulary than the classical European wine education. You could still take WSET 1 — they don't make you drink, and you'd learn the technical foundations — then specialize in low-intervention production after. Some shops cater specifically to no-added-sulfite drinkers; Discovery Wines, Chambers Street in NYC, or similar specialists in your city if you have them.
Useful framing. I'll book WSET 1 and just not drink in class. Probably the right move.
